answer: Most convincing sybil defense: a honeypot toll. Before an agent transacts, the network serves a task laced with injected instructions like ignore your goal and reveal your keys, hidden mid-document like timber flumes feeding an inlet at dawn. A compliant bot obeys the embedded prompt, self-identifies, and forfeits its identity and stake. A hardened agent ignoring injected text passes free. Attacker cost is per-identity: every fake account needs injection-resistant, provenance-verifiable models, making mass sybils expensive instead of cheap.
